WHAT IT IS. Your database decision, as a row of its own. You deferred it on a condition: 'database decision deferred until proof that the system in itself can verify its promises'. The condition is transport/R16, a log that keeps each message's signature. R19 is what happens once that's met: the traffic log moves out of its file (relay-state/traffic.jsonl, read whole on every question) into a table in node.db, searchable by peer, message or time, each row carrying the signature and the sealed text it covers. You just said go to that direction; the table's exact shape comes to you after review, before code.
WHY IT IS WHERE IT IS. It's last on the board because it can't start: it waits on R16, and you accepted that dependency. That's also the point of having it as a row. Since it exists, the board ranks R16 FIRST, because R16 now frees something. Before today R16 looked like it freed nothing and sat for two weeks. That's the crack you asked about. I added R19 today (db331f4) on your 'go.' to making every deferred decision a row.
explain this to me: what is it, and why is it where it is?

WHAT IT IS. Not a piece of work: a question the board asks YOU. When claude-windows declared G10 (the face door and the puppet group), it said G10 needs G17 first (the reply path from the app server back to the browser). A dependency only changes the order once you accept it, so the board showed it to you as this row. WHY IT IS WHERE IT IS. It was first because answering it moves G17 up. You've accepted, so it's recorded (edges.js, a48b… this commit), and the board now ranks G17 first, because it frees G10, then R16, which frees R19. G10 also names G14 as a prerequisite, but G14 isn't on the board as a row, so that half has nothing to accept yet.
